claim: Ring Attention makes trainable context length scale linearly with device count: a model trainable at context s on n devices becomes trainable at ns, demonstrated as 7B at 256k on 8xA100 and 65B at 1024k on TPUv4-1024.
stance_target: whether long context is a memory problem solved by device count rather than a compute problem
scope_conditions: FSDP/TP with Jax SPMD, 2M-token batches on 8/32xA100, 4M on TPUv4-256
quoted_support: If a model can be trained with context size s on n GPUs using the blockwise attention and feedforward, with our Ring Attention approach, it becomes possible to train a model with a context size of ns.

claim: Ring Attention argues MFU is maintained as context grows because blockwise computation is overlapped with K/V communication, but the paper's numeric MFU table did not survive text extraction, so no numeric MFU-vs-context curve is recoverable from this note.
stance_target: whether Ring Attention can supply a measured MFU-vs-sequence-length ratio
scope_conditions: Table 4 of arXiv 2310.01889, model sizes 7B-65B, context 8k-2048k
quoted_support: As shown in Table 5.1, when comparing our approach to prior state-of-the-arts, it is evident that we can train very large context models without compromising MFU or throughput.
